chapters.title: The One Rule
chapters.tease: Every organisation has a theory about why it is slow.

chapters.title: A Fleet, Not a Tool
chapters.tease: Most people meet agents as tools.

chapters.title: What Counts as a Change
chapters.tease: A number like 77,000 changes a month invites an obvious suspicion.

chapters.title: Waiting for the Engine
chapters.tease: Spawn was founded in 2024 around one question: how do you build a machine that benefits most as tokens get smarter, faster and cheaper?

chapters.title: Small Team, Large Fleet
chapters.tease: When the founder first saw the token bill, he had the reaction any sensible person would have: we must be doing something wrong.

chapters.title: The Square of Small Talk
chapters.tease: The first thing that broke when Spawn's fleet came alive was conversation.

chapters.title: Ants Do Not Hold Stand-ups
chapters.tease: Ants solved the coordination problem long before anyone invented the stand-up.

chapters.title: The End of the Pull Request
chapters.tease: Earlier in 2026 Spawn got rid of pull requests.

chapters.title: Messy Within the Hour
chapters.tease: If every change has to be perfect before it lands, you have reinvented the queue.

chapters.title: Fix Forward
chapters.tease: Human teams fix things backwards.

chapters.title: Production Is the Test Bed
chapters.tease: With the talking removed, the next wait Spawn found was people.

chapters.title: The Bug That Files Itself
chapters.tease: Savi, the assistant inside Spawn that helps people make games, files bugs herself.

chapters.title: Hyper Observability
chapters.tease: For the rest of the loop, Spawn uses a phrase the founder calls hyper observability.

chapters.title: Money Has Sensors Too
chapters.tease: Spawn's agents watch more than the product.

chapters.title: An Hour Without a Ship
chapters.tease: A loop this tight only works if it keeps turning, so Spawn treats an hour without a release as a SEV-0 , its most serious class of incident.

chapters.title: Seven Hundred Questions Before Breakfast
chapters.tease: By October the only thing still waiting at Spawn was taste, and most of it was the founder's.

chapters.title: The Judge Reads the Minutes
chapters.tease: Every conversation Spawn had held for two years was sitting in the repository as text.

chapters.title: Saying No to Working Code
chapters.tease: So what do the humans do?

chapters.title: Ask for a Hundred Times
chapters.tease: The second human job the founder calls entropy : asking the model for things it would not think of on its own.

chapters.title: Delete What the Last Model Needed
chapters.tease: Every generation of models arrives with a gift and a bill.

chapters.title: Run Your First Waits Audit
chapters.tease: Everything so far has been someone else's company.

chapters.title: Three Tiers of Trust
chapters.tease: Spawn's risk appetite is not yours, and should not be.

chapters.title: Client Work Is Not a Game
chapters.tease: The method works anywhere.

chapters.title: Spawning an Agent Properly
chapters.tease: The moment the fleet idea lands, everyone wants a new agent.

chapters.title: The Organisation That Ships
chapters.tease: The founder of Spawn thinks large companies will find all this hard to adopt, and his reason is not technical.
